title: The Pale Protocol
premise: Edmund Joubert, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Pale Anchor, has spent twelve years hauling cargo through contested orbits between two warring orbital powers. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, Edmund discovers the flicker was a handshake: an ancient alien protocol waking beneath the station, offering to preserve one half of humanity in cryosleep while it 'prunes' the other to stabilize a collapsing ecosystem. As factions race to seize the Protocol's control core, Edmund — who has belonged to no one for twelve years — becomes the only person both sides trust enough to arbitrate. In the end, Edmund refuses the binary entirely, sacrificing their own place among the saved to rewire the Protocol into a lottery open to all, and dies alone on Pale Anchor as humanity wakes together into a smaller, humbler future.
about_author: Gideon Galloway is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years stationed on remote North Atlantic platforms before turning to fiction. Their work explores isolation, machinery, and the strange tenderness that grows between people and the systems that keep them alive.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Weight
chapters.summary: Edmund Joubert's routine cargo haul is interrupted when gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine — twelve years of solitude have made Edmund fluent in noticing what machines ignore.

chapters.title: The Last Human on Pale Anchor
chapters.summary: A portrait of Edmund's life: maintenance logs, synthetic meals, one-way messages from a sister who stopped replying years ago. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like a uniform; belonging reduced to a station that needs them.

chapters.title: Anomalies in the Ballast
chapters.summary: Edmund traces the gravitational flicker to mass readings that don't add up — something enormous and dense beneath the station's keel. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Voices in Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Both warring powers — the Meridian Combine and the Halcyon Compact — hail Pale Anchor simultaneously, each claiming the anomaly. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: being noticed after years of invisibility feels less like rescue than capture.

chapters.title: What the Keel Remembers
chapters.summary: Edmund descends into sealed sublevels predating human occupation and finds geometric corridors that predate every colonial record. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: vertigo of scale — humanity is a tenant, not an owner.

chapters.title: The Word That Wakes
chapters.summary: A dormant interface responds to Edmund's touch, speaking in a language assembled from twelve years of Edmund's own maintenance logs. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: intimacy with the inhuman — the machine learned them.

chapters.title: Terms of Preservation
chapters.summary: The entity — the Protocol — reveals its function: it can cryo-preserve half of all humans while culling the rest to rebalance the dying biosphere. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: horror delivered with perfect courtesy.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest: Eight Billion
chapters.summary: Edmund runs the numbers: the Protocol's capacity, the population, the arithmetic of halves. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: guilt of the accountant — someone must do this math, and no one else can see it yet.

chapters.title: The Combine Arrives
chapters.summary: A Meridian warship docks uninvited; its captain, Ilsa Voss, offers Edmund protection and partnership. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: warmth offered with a hook inside it.

chapters.title: The Compact Objects
chapters.summary: Halcyon envoys broadcast accusations: Meridian knew about the Protocol first and hid it. POV: alternating Edmund and intercepted broadcasts. Emotional beat: paranoia — every voice now sounds scripted.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Edmund came to Pale Anchor fleeing a family scandal, trading community for exile. POV: Edmund (past). Emotional beat: understanding why belonging terrifies them more than loneliness.

chapters.title: Voss's Bargain
chapters.summary: Captain Voss proposes Meridian control the selection criteria — 'rationally,' she says — and wants Edmund as the neutral technician of record. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: temptation of purpose; corruption dressed as competence.

chapters.title: Sabotage in Section Nine
chapters.summary: Someone sabotages the station's cooling grid; Edmund nearly dies repairing it and suspects neither fleet did it. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: fear that the Protocol itself is testing them.

chapters.title: The Third Signal
chapters.summary: Edmund discovers a third faction: descendants of station crews who went dark decades ago, living in the deep corridors beside the Protocol. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: shock of finding people where there should be none — belonging ambushes them.

chapters.title: Children of the Keel
chapters.summary: The deep-dwellers, led by an old engineer named Amara Okonkwo, have coexisted with the Protocol for two generations. POV: Edmund and Amara. Emotional beat: tentative kinship; Edmund eats at a table for the first time in years.

chapters.title: What Amara Knows
chapters.summary: Amara reveals the Protocol has run this cycle before on other worlds — and that 'half' is negotiable only to whoever holds its core. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: inherited grief; her people survived by staying small and quiet.

chapters.title: Fleet Mobilization
chapters.summary: Both fleets begin moving on Pale Anchor; diplomacy collapses over a disputed boarding incident. POV: multiple, via Edmund monitoring comms. Emotional beat: dread of inevitability — history repeating at orbital scale.

chapters.title: The Ethics of a Switch
chapters.summary: Edmund drafts selection frameworks at Voss's request and hates how easily the mind accepts the task. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: self-disgust — power corrupting not through cruelty but through paperwork.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Refusal
chapters.summary: Amara rejects every framework: her people will not choose, will not be chosen, will hide again if they must. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: stubborn dignity against impossible math.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Combine and Compact marines clash in the docking ring; forty die in eleven minutes. POV: Edmund, hiding in the vents. Emotional beat: trauma — the abstract halves become bodies.

chapters.title: The Core Room
chapters.summary: Edmund finally reaches the Protocol's heart: a chamber where gravity pools like water and time feels thick. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: awe — standing inside the thing deciding everyone's fate.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Voss and the Compact's Admiral Reyes meet aboard Pale Anchor under truce, each demanding Edmund hand over access codes. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: crushing weight of being the hinge everyone leans on.

chapters.title: A Name in Every Slot
chapters.summary: Under pressure, Edmund enters names into the preservation ledger — beginning with their estranged sister — and realizes they cannot stop halfway. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: corruption completed quietly, one loving name at a time.

chapters.title: Amara's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Amara threatens to destroy the core rather than let either fleet own it; Edmund must choose sides or find another way. POV: Edmund and Amara. Emotional beat: love and fury entangled — the first person to feel like family may burn everything.

chapters.title: Betrayal Aboard
chapters.summary: Voss's aide attempts to seize the core during a shift change; Amara's people take casualties shielding Edmund. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: grief and clarity — the fleets will never share, and neither will the Protocol.

chapters.title: The Protocol Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: The entity explains its true constraint: it doesn't require half — it requires a decision made by a human who understands the cost. That was always the test. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: revelation — the flicker chose Edmund twelve seconds ago.

chapters.title: Why Me
chapters.summary: Edmund interrogates the Protocol's choice: isolated, unaligned, practiced in small kindnesses to machines. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: bitter recognition — their exile was their qualification.

chapters.title: Countdown to Cull
chapters.summary: With no decision entered, the Protocol begins default protocols; both fleets prepare final assault. POV: multiple via Edmund. Emotional beat: ticking-clock panic; every option closes except one nobody wants.

chapters.title: The Lottery Proposal
chapters.summary: Edmund proposes rewiring the Protocol: universal random selection, no arbiter, no exemptions — including themselves. POV: Edmund, pitching to Voss, Reyes, and Amara. Emotional beat: desperate hope — fairness as the only argument left.

chapters.title: Reyes Blinks
chapters.summary: Admiral Reyes, shown the casualty projections, becomes the first leader to accept the lottery publicly. POV: Reyes then Edmund. Emotional beat: fragile relief — power yielding, once, to arithmetic.

chapters.title: Voss's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Voss offers Edmund immortality-adjacent privilege: guaranteed slots for anyone Edmund names, in exchange for Meridian oversight. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the last and sweetest temptation — save your sister, betray everyone.

chapters.title: Sister, Awake
chapters.summary: Edmund's sister, revived briefly from civilian cryo to testify, tells Edmund she'd rather roll the dice than be chosen. POV: sister, then Edmund. Emotional beat: reconciliation and release — love means refusing to be exempt.

chapters.title: Mutiny on Pale Anchor
chapters.summary: Voss moves to take the core by force; Amara's people, Compact defectors, and Edmund's sabotage delay her in the deep corridors. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: solidarity forged in fire — the exile finally fights alongside others.

chapters.title: Rewiring God
chapters.summary: In the core room, Edmund and Amara rewrite the Protocol's selection logic while Voss's forces breach the outer doors. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: transcendent focus — a technician's hands doing the most important work in human history.

chapters.title: The Price of the Rewrite
chapters.summary: The rewire requires a human consciousness as its checksum — someone must remain merged with the core permanently. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: quiet devastation; Edmund volunteers before anyone else can.

chapters.title: Lottery Night
chapters.summary: Across the system, every living human is entered; the draw executes as fleets stand down mid-assault. POV: sweeping, anchored in Edmund inside the core. Emotional beat: terrible serenity — randomness as mercy.

chapters.title: What Voss Did Next
chapters.summary: Defeated, Voss chooses to enter the lottery rather than flee — her final act of faith in the system she tried to corrupt. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: redemption at the edge; even the corrupt submit to fairness.

chapters.title: The Long Goodbye
chapters.summary: As cryo-bays fill, Edmund — distributed now through the station — says goodbye to Amara, who chooses to stay awake as the new keeper. POV: Edmund and Amara. Emotional beat: tender farewell; belonging achieved at the moment of leaving.

chapters.title: Waking Together
chapters.summary: Years later, the survivors wake to a pruned but healing world, governed by no one, owing everything to a lottery and a ghost in a relay station. POV: Amara and new generations. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal — survival without innocence.

chapters.title: Pale Anchor, Still Burning
chapters.summary: The final image: Pale Anchor holding orbit, its lights steady, Edmund's consciousness keeping watch over the traffic lanes — no longer the last human, but the first of something new. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: peace — alone at last, and no longer lonely.
